answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks with a staked identity trellis: every participant locks collateral and is woven into random cross-check groups, so a forked identity must post the same bond as a genuine one. Trust is read from a signed signal of past work, weighted sublinearly per unique key, so an attacker's fake keys add almost no extra sway. A fresh ember token must be re-earned each round by paying fees, so keeping thousands of phantom nodes alive burns real funds, while any caught duplicate is slashed.
